content.text: (⍉able to do): ipsilat cerebellar lesion (cerebellar hemisphere dysfun), basal ganglia dz(Parkinson's), upper motor neuron (UMN) lesions
: contralat corticospinal tract or ipsilat cerebellar patho
Finger to finger, finger to nose:
Smooth, accurate, equal B/L; no tremor
(past-pointing): Overshooting or undershooting target; ipsilateral cerebellar lesion
(Tremor worsens on approach): cerebellar dysfunction (contrasts with resting tremor of Parkinson's)
rregular or veering path): ipsilateral cerebellar hemisphere or P. column (sensory ataxia) lesion
: Focal cerebellar or UMN lesion on affected side
Heel to shin, heel to toe
1. Rise from seated position: w/o using arms to push up (cross arms across chest)
3. Walk heel-to-toe in straight line (tandem walking)
posture, step, stance, balance, swinging of arms & mvt of legs (stumble, fall, lack of musc control)
Cerebellar dysfun; worse w tandem walking
P. column/proprioceptive loss; worse in dark or w eyes closed.
UMN lesion (stroke); affected leg swing out
(shuffling, festinating, ↓arm swing, stooped): Basal ganglia dysfun
(hip drop): Gluteus medius weak (hip abductors); L5 radiculopathy or hip patho
: Shortened stance on painful limb; msk patho
- Feet together, eyes open initially, then close both eyes for 3
Protect pt from falls during test
: Little to no swaying; maintain  upright posture & balance
: Swaying, loss of balance, side stepping-esp w eyes closed, poss normal balance w eyes open
: difficulty standing w feet together -eyes open or closed
: Intact proprioception + cerebellar func + vestibular input
(worse eyes closed, okay eyes open) -Sensory ataxia: Indicates posterior column/proprioceptive deficit (e.g., peripheral neuropathy, subacute combined degeneration, tabes dorsalis)
(falls with eyes open OR closed): Cerebellar dz; pt ⍉compensate even w vision.
: Consistent directional fall toward side of lesion w eyes closed
- Arms extended at shoulder level, w hands supinated, hold position for
- ↑effect: close eyes or press on 1 forearms
Abnormal: Unable to hold position, pronation/“drift”/lower ±1 arm
Contralat UMN (corticospinal tract) lesion - stroke, TIA, MS, tumor –Pronation pattern reflects flexor-extensor imbalance of UMN weakness
: May indicate early or evolving UMN pathology; also useful to detect subclinical hemiparesis.
cerebellar dysfun or proprioceptive deficit -sensory ataxia
